:::{#rem-overfitting-tradeoff}
#### Overfitting and the trade-off

By @thm-epe-decomposition,
$\epe{\candproc{\icand}}{\nobs}{\predvar}$ is the squared bias plus the variance plus $\varpar$.
Under a [bias--variance trade-off](#def-bias-variance-tradeoff)
among $\candproc{1}, \ldots, \candproc{\ncand}$,
moving from $\candproc{\icand}$ to $\candproc{\icand + 1}$
lowers the expected squared prediction error at $\predvar$
when the squared bias falls by more than the variance rises,
and raises it otherwise.
The smallest of $\epe{\candproc{1}}{\nobs}{\predvar}, \ldots, \epe{\candproc{\ncand}}{\nobs}{\predvar}$
is often at some $\candproc{\icand}$ with $1 < \icand < \ncand$
[@james2021islr2e, sec. 2.2.2],
but not always:
if the mean function $\mean$ is a candidate of $\candproc{1}$,
the squared bias of $\candproc{1}$ can be zero,
and then no later $\candproc{\icand}$ has a smaller squared bias
and, under the trade-off, none has a smaller variance,
so none has a smaller expected squared prediction error.
Past the smallest error,
the candidates have lowered their squared bias by less than they have raised their variance,
and their fitted models tend to [overfit](#def-overfitting):
they fit their training sets more closely than the fitted model of the candidate with the smallest error
but predict new observations worse.

:::
